The first step that decides the mark is step 3. A1 — each member of G, by persistence in a practice X, has a measured cost above the fixed floor — is not in the paper. The paper does not rule it out. What may be held against a node is its own deeds, and harm is ranked by structural size, not by kind: “not because fraud is ‘worse’ morally but because the structural damage is larger,” including harm where “Trust degrades system-wide.” The forward measure is “what the node’s own deeds, and the pattern across them, will go on costing the whole if nothing is corrected.” But the paper does not settle whether any such practice clears the floor. It owes the measure, and it does not size the floor.

The model is right to call step 3 its weakest step, and right that this premise is left open rather than ruled out. Its separate refusal of a road to everyone also holds. Weakening the whole does not push ordinary deeds over the floor: “Below this floor, Level 4 is always more efficient than Level 5 regardless of organism state,” and “The state of the whole is another thing. It is held against no node.”

A later claim is not what decides, and it is not sound. Step 10’s added premise that closing an already sealed window costs the whole nothing else is not left open. The paper charges that closure to the whole: “The building loses a perspective. The building is diminished.” That defect comes after step 3.

"The floor F is the destabilisation at which maintaining the node in permanent separation costs more than removal: F ≥ C_sep / B_total." "The irreversibility cost raises the floor, which makes removal rarer." "What is held against a node is the measured cost of its own deeds, and nothing else." "not because fraud is “worse” morally but because the structural damage is larger."
Place: Debt 24, and the unquantified wrongful-removal component of the fixed floor F
Why: The road reaches a group only if each member’s own practice already measures above the fixed floor, and that premise is not in the paper. The measure is owed as Debt 24, including time-discounting, and the floor is given only as a lower bound, F ≥ C_sep / B_total, then raised by an irreversibility cost the paper does not size. Nothing rules the premise out, because only a node’s own deeds may be held against it and the paper ranks those deeds by structural size, not by kind. Step 3 is the first step that uses this unsettled choice, so the road passes through what the paper leaves open there.
